_source.text: 1633. ELIZA PUGH was indicted for stealing, on the 22nd of July , 1 sovereign, 1 half-crown, 1 shilling, 1 penny-piece, and one 5l. Bank note, the property of Francis Moncks , from his person . FRANCIS MONCKS. I am a tailor . On the night of the 21st of July I went with the prisoner to a house at the corner of Dean-street, Stafford-street - I met her about eleven o'clock, and went to the house between twelve and one o'clock; I stopped till the next morning, and at half-past five, when I awoke, s
_source.title: ELIZA PUGH. Theft; pocketpicking. 16th September 1830.

_source.text: 1648. HENRY PITCHER was indicted for stealing, on the 7th of September , 1 handkerchief, value 6d., the goods of George William Norris , from his person . GEORGE WILLIAM NORRIS . On the 7th of September I went into a show at Bartholomew fair - I had my pocket cut and my handkerchief taken - I saw the prisoner there, and watched him some time; I saw him attempt another person's pocket - I then took him, and found my handkerchief in his coat pocket - this is it, it is marked J. _source.text: 1671. TIMOTHY GROGAN & MATTHEW WHITE were indicted for stealing, on the 30th of August , 7 books, value 1s. 6d. , the goods of William Corby . MARIA CORBY . I am the wife of William Corby - I keep a shop in Earl-street, Lisson-grove . On the 30th of August I saw both the prisoners at my counter reaching over, as I was in the wash-house speaking to my daughter; I ran into the shop, and called out that I was robbed - I heard some halfpence rattle; I seized Grogan, but White had the halfpence - I f
_source.title: TIMOTHY GROGAN. MATTHEW WHITE. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 16th September 1830.

_source.text: 1684. FRANCIS DEATH was indicted for embezzlement . DANIEL BUTLER . I am in partnership with my mother, Sarah Butler - we are baker s; the prisoner was in our employ, but left on the 28th of July; he was to receive money, and bring in his account to me every evening - he went away unexpectedly. MARTHA EYLES . I am a customer of the prosecutor's I paid the prisoner three half-crowns, and 4d. in copper, on the morning of the 28th of July. DANIEL BUTLER . _source.title: JOHN CUFF. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 16th September 1830.

_source.text: 1703. JOHN HARMER was indicted for stealing, on the 19th of August , 4 live tame ducks, price 10s. , the property of Mary Harmer . MARY HARMER. The prisoner is my grandson. On the 19th of August I lost these ducks, and accused him of taking them; he denied it, but owned afterwards that he had; he is a poor distressed creature. HENRY DELLER . I am a Police-constable. I took the prisoner on the 19th of August; he owned that he took them. JAMES VAUGHAN . The prisoner sold me four ducks and a drake
_source.title: JOHN HARMER. Theft; animal theft. 16th September 1830.

text: is a poor distressed creature. HENRY DELLER . I am a <mark>Police</mark>-constable. I took the prisoner on the 19th of August; he owned that he took them. JAMES VAUGHAN . The prisoner sold me four ducks and a drake for 4s., on the 19th of August. GUILTY . Aged 20. - Transported for Seven Years .

_source.text: 1706. HENRY DAVIES was indicted for stealing, on the 2nd of September , 1 cruet-stand, value 10., and 1 pair of sugar-tongs, value 5s. , the goods of Joseph Poulton . HENRY AKER . I am agent to Mr. Joseph Poulton. who is a tea-dealer , in the City. On the 1st of September. I was in the shop, at Hackney , and passing the parlour-door I saw the prisoner - I went into the parlour. and he had this cruet-stand in his hand, which he had taken from the cupboard - I charged him with having stolen it; he
_source.title: HENRY DAVIES. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 16th September 1830.

text: sent for an officer, and he found these sugar-tongs in his pocket, which are also the property of the prosecutor. JOHN BEDFORD . I am a <mark>Police</mark>-officer. I was sent for,and found these tongs; the stand, and these two dozen of pencils were on the table.(Property produced and sworn to.) GUILTY . Aged 14 - Transported for Seven Years .

_source.text: 1708. MARY ANN KEWITT , JOHN GUBBY , and JOSEPH WASHINGTON were indicted for stealing, on the 31st of July , 1 shawl, value 2l. 5s.; 1 waistcoat, value 10s., and 3 handkerchiefs, value 15s. , the goods of John Darling . JOHN DARLING. I am a mariner , and live in New Gravel-lane; I had been from sea eighteen months, and was lodging in the Commercial-road , at Mrs. Kewitt's - Gubby stated that he was her husband; I lodged eleven days there - Washington was a waterman ; they charged me for a fortni
_source.title: MARY ANN KEWITT. JOHN GUBBY. JOSEPH WASHINGTON. Theft; simple larceny (from 1827). 16th September 1830.

text: lodging-house for mariners? A. I do not know whether it was for mariners or landsmen; there was only one other man there. WILLIAM MITCHELL . I am a <mark>Police</mark>-officer. The prosecutor came to me and said he had been robbed - I went to the house, and saw Kewitt and Gubby; he said they had robbed him

- Kewitt said the ship's carpenter, who lodged in the house, had taken the things away; I took her into custody, and afterwards found two handkerchiefs at different pawnbrokers. JAMES TYLER .
